Subject: Procurement questionnaire: uptime/latency SLOs and observability access

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed with throughput and the routing controls. Procurement asked me to send a short, targeted questionnaire we need to close out before we can finalize our procurement packet. Can you provide answers for the following? We only need concise, factual responses.

1) SLO definitions and windows: What are the exact uptime and p50/p99 latency SLOs you commit to at the hosted API tier? Please state measurement windows (30d/90d) and how unavailable periods are counted.
2) Measurement: Which metrics do you use to measure the SLOs (endpoint-level 1xx/2xx/5xx counts, token-level latency, infra health signals)? Where are these metrics computed (control plane vs. edge)?
3) Monitoring & alerting: What are threshold policies and who receives incident alerts for customer-impacting degradations? Do you provide pager escalation for enterprise accounts?
4) Customer access: Can customers view raw SLO metrics and historical dashboards? If so, what access level (read-only dashboard, API keys, metrics export)? Any restrictions for hosted vs. dedicated/private deployments?
5) Exceptions & credits: Describe how exceptions are requested/approved and the credit calculation for missed SLOs. Typical SLA language is fine.
6) Evidence: Can you provide instrumentation evidence (sample dashboards, retention windows, data retention policy) and SOC2/audit artifacts?

If you can return this by EOD Monday (1/12) that would help our timeline.

Best,
Amit
Amit Shah
Senior Procurement Manager
BrightBridge Health

Hi Amit,

Thanks — attaching a short packet that addresses each item. Summary below; attached PDF has exact metric names, PromQL snippets, and sample dashboard links.

1) SLOs & windows: Hosted API (standard tier): Uptime SLO = 99.95% measured on a 30-day rolling window; p50 latency SLO = 80ms, p99 latency SLO = 450ms measured on token-delivery latency per-request over 30-day rolling window. Dedicated contracts can be defined in the order form (we commonly set 99.99% for higher tiers). Unavailable periods are taken from control-plane-aggregated endpoint health and exclude scheduled maintenance windows with 48h notice.

2) Measurement: Primary signals: HTTP status codes (2xx/5xx), request-level token latency, and per-inference VM health (GPU heartbeat). SLO computation is performed in our control plane (time-series engine) which ingests region-edge metrics; raw edge metrics are retained for 90 days, aggregated SLO time series for 13 months. Sample PromQL and metric names are attached.

3) Monitoring & alerting: Default thresholds: - Uptime degradation alert at <99.8% over 1h rolling window; - Severity-1 pager when p99 latency > 2x baseline for >10 minutes causing client errors; - Customer-facing status page incidents for degradations >5 minutes. Enterprise customers receive an on-call escalation list (email+pager) via our incident manager as part of the dedicated onboarding.

4) Customer access: We provide read-only dashboard access for hosted customers through the Redwood Console (per-tenant RBAC). Dashboards can be exported (CSV/JSON) and we offer a metrics export API for enterprise/partner integrations. For Dedicated/Private deployments, customers can choose to host the observability stack or receive the same read-only console access depending on network configuration (VPC peering or private links).

5) Exceptions & credits: Exceptions follow a formal request: customer opens a support ticket with timeline, impact, and mitigation. For hosted plans, SLA credits are pro-rated monthly: Credit = (SLA target - measured uptime)/SLA target * monthly invoice for the affected service, capped at 50% for a single month (standard). We provide options for service credits or one-time bill adjustments; credits require corroborating telemetry which we can share.

6) Evidence: Attached: "slo-measurement-answers.pdf" (PromQL snippets, retention policy, sample dashboard screenshots) and a short text file with steps to request read-only access. SOC2 and audit artifacts are available upon execution of our standard non-disclosure and evidence access agreement; we can start a gated evidence share immediately.

Attachment: slo-measurement-answers.pdf (PDF, 54KB)
Attachment: dashboard-readonly-access-instructions.txt (TXT, 2KB)

Happy to hop on a short call if you want us to walk through the PromQL and the example dashboards.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Team,

BrightBridge has three clarifications (region-level SLA aggregation, service-account export access, cross-period credit calculation). My proposed answers below — please confirm or edit before I send back to Amit:

1) Global SLA aggregation: We will state that hosted global endpoints present a single customer-facing SLA aggregated across active regional endpoints; failovers are included in that aggregation unless the customer has opted into a dedicated regional contract. (Implication: we treat cross-region failover as part of the same SLA for hosted customers.)

2) Service account exports: We can offer a read-only service account scoped to metrics export with OAuth tokens and 90-day rotation recommended. For enterprise customers we support client-credential flows with scoped API tokens and capability to rotate via KMS — rotation policy is negotiable but 90 days is our default. We should offer an operations onboarding checklist.

3) Cross-period credits: The pro-rated formula will be the same; if an incident overlaps billing periods we calculate credit per affected invoice month using the measured uptime for that invoice period (standard accounting practice). We cap aggregated credits to 50% per invoice month.

Do you want me to include a short excerpt of the credit calc example (numbers) or keep at high level? Also, Lauren — for SOC2 evidence gating, confirm the current steps for evidence share (NDA then secure evidence folder).

Thanks,
Marissa
